post.description:
Sign in or sign up with Google OAuth.

Flow:
1. Frontend gets authorization code from Google Sign-In redirect
2. Backend exchanges code for access token via Google's token endpoint
3. Backend fetches user info from Google's userinfo endpoint
4. If email exists in our DB: login (link Google ID if not already linked)
5. If email is new: create user, mark email verified, profile_completed=False
6. Return JWT tokens + user profile + is_new flag

Exchange a valid refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token.
Security: the old refresh token is revoked and a new one is issued (token rotation)
to limit the replay window if a refresh token is stolen.
Revoke a refresh token (logout from one device).

Create a CLI auth session. The CLI generates a session_id,
opens the browser, and polls /cli-session/{id} until the user logs in.

Complete a CLI auth session. Called by the frontend after the user logs in.
Generates tokens and stores them in the session for the CLI to poll.

post.description:

The token is a JWT with purpose="email_verify" and the user ID as subject.

Generate a new email verification token for the authenticated user.
Requires a valid access token. Logs the verification URL (email sending TBD).

Generate a password reset token. Always returns 200 regardless of whether
the email exists (prevents email enumeration attacks).

Reset a user's password using a signed token.
Revokes all existing refresh tokens for the user (forces re-login everywhere).

Begin TOTP 2FA setup for the authenticated user.

Generates a new TOTP secret, encrypts it, stores it, and returns the secret
along with a QR code URI and 10 one-time recovery codes.

If 2FA is already enabled, this overwrites the pending (unconfirmed) setup.
If 2FA is already confirmed, the user must disable it first.

Confirm 2FA setup by verifying a TOTP code from the user's authenticator app.

The user must have called /auth/2fa/setup first. This endpoint verifies the code
against the stored (encrypted) secret and activates 2FA if valid.

Disable 2FA for the authenticated user.

post.description:
Generate new recovery codes, replacing the old ones.

Requires a valid TOTP code (not a recovery code) for verification.
Returns 10 new plaintext codes: the user must save them securely.

Complete the 2FA login flow by verifying a TOTP code or recovery code.

This endpoint is UNAUTHENTICATED: the user provides the challenge_token
from the login response plus their 2FA code. On success, real access and
refresh tokens are issued.

Accepts either:
  - A 6-digit TOTP code from the authenticator app
  - A recovery code in XXXX-XXXX-XXXX format (consumed on use: single use only)

Rate limited to 5/minute to prevent brute force attacks.

delete.description:
Delete (anonymize) the current user's account (GDPR Article 17).

This endpoint performs a soft-delete by anonymizing the user's profile
rather than hard-deleting, to preserve leaderboard and submission integrity.

Process:
  1. Verify password confirmation
  2. Anonymize profile fields (name, email, bio, etc.)
  3. Invalidate password hash
  4. Deactivate account (is_active = False)
  5. Delete messages, notifications, and forum post content
  6. Revoke all refresh tokens (force logout everywhere)
  7. Log deletion in audit log

Submissions and leaderboard entries are preserved but now show "Deleted User".

GroupLeaderboardOut.description: Full group leaderboard response for a challenge phase.

GroupMemberOut.title: GroupMemberOut
GroupMemberOut.description: Group member with denormalized user info for display.

GroupOut.title: GroupOut
GroupOut.description: Group summary with member count: used in list endpoints.

JoinRequest.title: JoinRequest
JoinRequest.description:
Request body for self-joining a challenge (POST /challenges/{slug}/members/join).
Optional message field for private challenges (admin sees this when reviewing).

LeaderboardEntryOut.title: LeaderboardEntryOut
LeaderboardEntryOut.description:
Single row on the leaderboard: one per user (best submission only).
metric_ranks is populated for mean_rank/weighted_rank methods: shows each
entry's per-metric rank (e.g. {"dice": 2, "hausdorff95": 5}).

LeaderboardOut.title: LeaderboardOut
LeaderboardOut.description: Full leaderboard response for a challenge phase.

MarketingConsentUpdate.title: MarketingConsentUpdate
MarketingConsentUpdate.description: Request body for PATCH /users/me/consent: update marketing email preference.

MemberInvite.title: MemberInvite
MemberInvite.description:
Request body for inviting a user to a challenge (POST /challenges/{slug}/members/invite).
Admin-only. The invited user gets status="pending" until they accept.

MemberOut.title: MemberOut
MemberOut.description: Challenge member with denormalized user info for display.

MemberUpdate.title: MemberUpdate
MemberUpdate.description:
Admin-only update of a member's role or status (PATCH /challenges/{slug}/members/{user_id}).
Used to approve/reject join requests or change roles.

MessageOut.title: MessageOut
MessageOut.description: A single message in a conversation.

NotificationReadRequest.title: NotificationReadRequest
NotificationReadRequest.description: Mark notifications as read: either specific IDs or all.

PermissionListOut.title: PermissionListOut
PermissionListOut.description: All available permissions grouped by category, for the frontend checkboxes.

SearchType.title: SearchType
SearchType.description: Allowed values for the 'type' query parameter.

SignupRequest.title: SignupRequest
SignupRequest.description:
Request body for POST /auth/signup.
Collects identity, affiliation, and policy acceptance (inspired by Grand Challenge).
All identity/affiliation fields are required for profile completeness.

SubmissionOut.title: SubmissionOut
SubmissionOut.description: Full submission details including evaluation results.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
Response from login/signup: includes both tokens and the user profile.
When requires_2fa is True, tokens are null and the client must complete
the 2FA challenge using the challenge_token at POST /auth/2fa/verify.

TwoFactorCodeRequest.title: TwoFactorCodeRequest
TwoFactorCodeRequest.description: Request body requiring a TOTP code (6 digits) or recovery code.

TwoFactorSetupResponse.title: TwoFactorSetupResponse
TwoFactorSetupResponse.description:
Response from 2FA setup: contains secret, QR URI, and one-time recovery codes.
The client should display the QR code and instruct the user to save recovery codes.

TwoFactorTokenResponse.title: TwoFactorTokenResponse
TwoFactorTokenResponse.description: Response from successful 2FA verification: real tokens issued.

TwoFactorVerifyRequest.title: TwoFactorVerifyRequest
TwoFactorVerifyRequest.description: Request body for completing 2FA login after password verification.

UserOut.title: UserOut
UserOut.description:
Full user representation returned by authenticated endpoints (e.g. GET /users/me).
Includes identity, affiliation, platform role, and verification status.
